name: WI-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+26 partisan lean makes it one of the most Democratic seats in Wisconsin
Longtime incumbent Gwen Moore has a large fundraising edge over an opponent with no reported finances
Prediction markets price a Democratic win near 95 percent
No general-election polls or expert ratings are available, limiting precision
model.rationale: The district's D+26 lean, Moore's incumbency, and her roughly $1.3 million raised against a challenger with no visible fundraising point to a margin in the high twenties, and markets price a Democratic win around 95 percent. With no polls or outside spending suggesting competition, the seat stays Safe Democratic.
model.watch: A late wave of outside spending against Moore or an unexpected personal scandal could narrow what is otherwise a lopsided district.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Gwen Moore, the longtime Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in this Milwaukee-based district, one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in Wisconsin with a partisan lean of D+26. She has raised about $1.3 million for the race, while Republican Tim Rogers shows no reported fundraising, and no outside groups are spending for or against either candidate. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the contest.

Prediction markets put Moore's chances around 95 percent, and the district's fundamentals point to a margin in the high twenties. Moore's relatively low cash on hand is a minor note, but with no visible challenger spending or outside opposition, the seat is rated Safe Democratic. An upset would require a shift well beyond anything currently evident in the race.
